source_text: Qui locus quam sit opinioni vestrae totus infestus, et primo opere disputatum est et, si quid hinc recoli oportuerit, disseretur. Nunc autem advertatur promissionem, quae facta est ad Abraham ob remunerationem fidei eius, in qua dicitur, quia pater multarum gentium constitueretur, ostendisse nec unius illum populi genitorem debere defendi, qui multarum gentium sit pater praedictus, nec ita solum credulitatis recepisse mercedem, ut alios similiter credentes a praemii consortio putetur excludere. Non est autem scriptum - inquit - tantummodo propter ipsum, quia reputatum est illi, sed et propter nos, quibus reputabitur credentibus in eum, qui suscitavit Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum a mortuis, qui traditus est propter delicta nostra et resurrexit propter iustificationem nostram [n217] .
pass_a_gloss: Which place how wholly hostile it is to your opinion has both been disputed in the first work and, if anything from this ought to be recalled, will be discussed. But now let it be noticed that the promise which was made to Abraham on account of a recompense of his faith, in which it is said that he would be constituted a father of many nations, showed both that he ought not to be defended as the begetter of one people, who was predicted as a father of many nations, and that he did not so only receive a wage of belief that he be thought to exclude others similarly believing from a consortium of the prize. But it was not written, he says, only on account of him, because it was reckoned to him, but also on account of us, to whom it will be reckoned believing in him who raised Jesus Christ our Lord from the dead, who was handed over on account of our offenses and rose on account of our justification.

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: How thoroughly this passage opposes your opinion was discussed in my first work; whatever needs to be recalled from it will be examined. For now, observe that the promise made to Abraham as a reward for his faith, saying that he would be established as the father of many nations, showed two things. He should not be maintained to be the progenitor of only one people, since he was foretold as the father of many nations. Nor did he receive the reward of belief so exclusively that others who believe in the same way should be thought excluded from sharing the reward. ‘But it was not written only for his sake,’ Paul says, ‘that it was reckoned to him, but also for ours, to whom it will be reckoned as we believe in the one who raised Jesus Christ our Lord from the dead, who was handed over because of our offenses and rose because of our justification’ (Romans 4:23–25).

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
